children: What Happened?
A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after a broad pickup in energy expenses lifted September inflation to 3.7%, surpassing expectations and driving bond yields higher.

The hotter-than-anticipated inflation reading dampened market sentiment across Wall Street, weighing heavily on major benchmark indexes and pulling equities down from recent highs. When inflation accelerates, it often increases expectations that borrowing costs will remain elevated for an extended period to curb economic overheating. Elevated interest rates can compress corporate valuations, particularly across growth sectors such as technology and semiconductors, where future earnings expectations play a central role in pricing.

Semiconductor shares faced extended pressure, marking their seventh consecutive session of declines as market participants recalibrated risk appetites. Beyond higher financing expenses, persistent energy-driven inflation risks squeezing operating margins and weakening broader enterprise spending. Investors are continuing to evaluate whether persistent price pressures will lead to tighter financial conditions and prolonged headwinds for capital-intensive industries.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.

children: Zooming In On Cognex (CGNX)

Cognex’s shares are quite volatile and have had 18 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 7 days ago when the stock dropped 7.5% on the news that rising Treasury yields and climbing oil prices dampened investor sentiment ahead of the release of the Federal Reserve's September meeting minutes. CNBC reported that Treasury yields climbed back to multiyear highs, ahead of the Federal Reserve’s September meeting minutes. The 10-year yield was up more than 3 basis points at 5.307% after touching its highest level since 2002, and the 30-year yield rose more than 4 basis points to 5.684% after hitting a 24-year high earlier. Policymakers raised interest rates in September for the first time since 2023, and traders are reading the minutes for clues on what comes next. CNBC also said the bond selloff has been tied to inflation worries and rising energy prices, with U.S. crude up 20% since the end of July. The stock was already under pressure from a Truist note earlier this week. According to TipRanks, Truist lowered its price target to $74 from $78 and kept a Hold rating in a preview of third-quarter results for industrial companies.

The firm said the setup into earnings looks constructive after a sector pullback tied to doubts about spending on power, data centers, and artificial intelligence, along with questions over who pays for power, local opposition, and project delays. Higher interest rates and elevated diesel and other input costs add to the near-term debate. Truist still expects company commentary to stay broadly constructive and for 2026 estimates to move higher.

Cognex is up 55.8% since the beginning of the year, but at $57.55 per share, it is still trading 20.5% below its 52-week high of $72.42 from June 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Cognex’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $694.20.
